fsm_states_server_transaction.name: WAIT_FOR_MB_INDICATION
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Idle state. Server waits for an incoming MODBUS request ADU. On RTU, end-of-frame is detected after ≥ 3.5 character-time silence; on ASCII, after CR LF; on TCP, after MBAP.Length bytes of PDU are received.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: VALIDATE_FUNCTION_CODE
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Check that the Function Code byte is supported by this server implementation. If not → ExceptionCode = 0x01 ILLEGAL FUNCTION.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: VALIDATE_DATA_ADDRESS
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Check that the Starting Address and Starting Address + Quantity - 1 lie within the server's table. If not → ExceptionCode = 0x02 ILLEGAL DATA ADDRESS.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: VALIDATE_DATA_VALUE
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Check that quantity, byte count, and value fields are within the per-function-code limits (e.g. Quantity ≤ 2000 for FC 1/2; ≤ 125 for FC 3/4; Output Value ∈ {0xFF00, 0x0000} for FC 5). If not → ExceptionCode = 0x03 ILLEGAL DATA VALUE.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: EXECUTE_MB_FUNCTION
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Perform the action: read or write the addressed bits / registers, run the diagnostic sub-function, or assemble the MEI response. If execution fails irrecoverably → ExceptionCode = 0x04 / 0x05 / 0x06 / 0x08.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: SEND_MODBUS_RESPONSE
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Compose a normal response PDU (function-code-dependent layout), prepend address/MBAP, append CRC/LRC if applicable, and transmit.

fsm_states_server_transaction.name: SEND_MODBUS_EXCEPTION_RESPONSE
fsm_states_server_transaction.description: Compose an exception PDU = (Function Code OR 0x80, Exception Code), prepend address/MBAP, append CRC/LRC, transmit.

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: BUILD_REQUEST
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: Client constructs PDU = Function Code + Data per function-code-specific layout, prepends Address (RTU/ASCII) or MBAP (TCP), appends CRC/LRC if serial.

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: TRANSMIT_REQUEST
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: Client sends the ADU on the chosen transport (UART for RTU/ASCII; TCP socket for TCP).

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: WAIT_FOR_RESPONSE
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: Client starts a request-timeout timer and waits for the response ADU.

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: RECEIVE_RESPONSE
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: On RTU/ASCII, wait for end-of-frame (T3.5 silence or CR LF). On TCP, read MBAP.Length bytes. Validate CRC / LRC / TCP checksum implicitly.

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: CLASSIFY_RESPONSE
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: If response function code MSB = 0 → normal response, decode response data. If MSB = 1 → exception response, read exception code, deliver error to application.

fsm_states_client_transaction.name: TIMEOUT
fsm_states_client_transaction.description: If no response within the configured timeout → report communication timeout to the application; client may retransmit or escalate.

fsm_hints.validation_order: Function code → Data address → Data value → Execute. The state diagram in Section 4.5 (Figure 9) of the spec mandates this order; an earlier check that passes does not waive a later check.
fsm_hints.broadcast_handling: On serial transports, Address 0 = broadcast: the server processes the request but does NOT send any response. Only commands that can be safely broadcast (some writes) should be sent with address 0; read codes are not broadcastable.
fsm_hints.abort_conditions: Communication error detected by the server (parity, framing, CRC, LRC mismatch) → silently discard the request; no exception response is sent. The client times out and may retransmit.
fsm_hints.no_response_class: Exception 0x05 ACKNOWLEDGE is returned for accepted-but-long-running programming commands so the client does NOT time out while the operation is in flight.

anti_deadlock_rule: Strict request/reply: only the client initiates; the server replies (or stays silent on broadcast / communication error). There is no scenario where both ends try to drive the bus simultaneously on a single-master / single-token network. On Modbus TCP with pipelined transactions, the MBAP.Transaction_ID lets the client correlate concurrent responses and prevents reply confusion.
exit_from_reset_or_power_up: After server power-up, all communication counters and the diagnostic register start cleared; data tables (Discrete Inputs / Coils / Input Registers / Holding Registers) hold their power-on defaults as defined by the device application. The server is ready to accept the first MODBUS request without further client-side initialization.

default_state_recommendation.serial_line_idle: Both directions idle (UART idle HIGH / TXD = mark) between frames.
default_state_recommendation.tcp_socket_initial: Client opens a TCP connection to server's port 502; server accepts; both sides ready to exchange MBAP-framed PDUs.

exception_response_logic.trigger: Any failed validation gate (function / address / value / execute).
exception_response_logic.pdu_layout: (Function Code OR 0x80, 1 B) + (Exception Code, 1 B). Total exception PDU = 2 bytes.
exception_response_logic.client_action: Inspect response.byte[0] MSB. If 1, treat as exception. Map exception code to user-facing error per Section 7 table.

diagnostics_listen_only_mode.trigger: FC 0x08 sub-function 0x0004 Force Listen Only Mode.
diagnostics_listen_only_mode.behavior: Server stops responding to all requests (no transmissions on the bus) until a Restart Communications Option sub-function (0x0001) is received.
diagnostics_listen_only_mode.rationale: Allows offline troubleshooting / wire tracing without affecting other devices on a multi-drop bus.

interrupt_priority_order: Not applicable at the protocol layer. Real implementations may prioritize incoming requests over outgoing responses or use OS-thread / interrupt-driven dispatch internally, but the spec does not define an interrupt-priority order.
